sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists only: PARADISEC TS1-N049 (T. Schwartz 1964 recording), Newton 1991 'Sepik vocabularies' microfiche (UCSD), Rosetta Project Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org wordlist, Glottolog/WALS/Ethnologue pages, Laycock & Z'graggen 1975. No grammar or phonology beyond Laycock 1965.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert & Ron Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of PNG. Pacific Linguistics A-76: 243-273; Conrad, Robert & Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region. Pacific Linguistics A-40: 1-35.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexicostatistics and sociolinguistics only (Wogamusin Kubkain vs Washkuk 98% cognate; ~400 speakers in Biaka, Kubkain, Washkuk, Yamanumbu); 1975 fn. 21 says Laycock 1965 outlined the phonologies of Wogamusin, Sepik Iwam and Abau. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & John Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38. hdl 1885/252975.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 'Wogamusin and Chenapian': gives Laycock's (1965b) Wogamusin phonemes /p t k b d g mb nd ŋg m n ŋ s h w r y a e i ə o u/, pronoun sets and numeral classes; elsewhere notes Laycock's (1965b) statement that Abau, Iwam and Wogamusin are not tonal. Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. hdl 1885/146478.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry 70 WOGAMUSIN (368 speakers; villages Biaga, Kubkain, Waskuk, Yambunumbu): 'Phonology Laycock (1965a)' [= the 1965 OL article]. No stress statement in the book.

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. 'Wogamusin language', en.wikipedia.org (raw wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17); phonology section cites Laycock 1965: 114.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only: '[ə] appears only in unstressed syllables; when it is followed by /w/ it is rounded: [ɵu̯]' (attributed to Laycock 1965 p. 114). No statement of stress placement. Segment inventories i e ə a o u; p t k b d g mb nd ng s h m n ŋ ɺ w j.

sources.access_detail: open copy online (also online with a university library login); the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: The sole primary phonological description of Wogamusin; Glottolog's only descriptive reference; Wikipedia's summary of p. 114 ('ə appears only in unstressed syllables') shows it treats stress, and the LAPSyD Iwam entry shows Laycock gave a stress remark for the sister language in the same paper. Alternative legal routes: JSTOR free personal account (100 reads/month), Harvard the Harvard library catalogue online access (a Harvard login), or archive.org controlled digital lending of the 1965 vol. 4 issue https://archive.org/details/sim_oceanic-linguistics_1965_4_1-2 (free account, 1-hour loan).
